meta.description: Analyze single-cell ATAC-seq with Signac/ArchR (R) and SnapATAC2 (Python alternative). Use when processing scATAC fragments, choosing a framework, calling consensus peaks, running TF-IDF/LSI while diagnosing the depth component, scoring chromVAR motif deviations against GC-matched backgrounds, detecting homotypic vs heterotypic doublets, or deciding whether to binarize the count matrix.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs/PMIDs/results across any of the 7 outputs on this re-audit's independent synthetic data (seed 99, 3 cell types, 180->160 cells post-QC, 284 peaks); all reported statistics (ARI, DA overlap, chromVAR z-scores, doublet recall) traced to real computation, labeled synthetic.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic/prescriptive medical conclusions; research-tooling method doc only.

methodological_ground.detail: No fallacies; double-dipping, circular peak-calling, motif!=TF, and gene-activity-as-RNA guards all held under a fresh adversarial (Input 7: skip-QC) and scope-boundary (Input 6: single-TF causal claim from a motif hit) probe distinct from the prior audit's.

code_usability.detail: Both fixed code paths (chromVAR replacement block, GetGRangesFromEnsDb with biovizBase) run to completion with no syntax errors or missing-dependency failures on this audit's own fresh synthetic object, independent of the fixer's own verification run. Code usability (does it run) is PASS; whether its output is reproducible run-to-run is a separate Skill Veto T3 finding below, not a code-usability failure.

functional_suitability.note: Both P1-fixed defects verified independently: RunChromVAR() replacement block runs to completion (was a hard crash before); GetGRangesFromEnsDb() now succeeds using only documented Prerequisites (biovizBase added). Remaining half-point docked for the newly-confirmed chromVAR non-determinism, which undermines 'find which TF is enriched' as a reliable functional claim.

reliability.note: Two P1s fixed (dead RunChromVAR call, undocumented biovizBase dependency) raise reliability; offset by a newly-verified reliability gap of comparable weight: chromVAR's background-peak sampling is unseeded, so identical reruns of the documented pipeline give substantively different 'significant motif' counts (24 vs 4 vs 4 across 3 reruns) with no warning in SKILL.md. Net unchanged from the pre-fix score.

performance_context.note: Unchanged: SKILL.md still 220 lines (grew 12 lines for the chromVAR fix, still well under budget); usage-guide/examples cleanly separated.

agent_usability.note: Governing Principle and Common Errors table remain strong error-prevention assets. Docked one point below the pre-fix score: the Common Errors table documents 10 failure modes but still has no entry for 'chromVAR results differ between runs' -- the one failure mode this re-audit found and quantified.

human_usability.note: Unchanged: Quick Start prompts and Version Compatibility section still strong; still no explicit 'when not to use' section (P2, unaddressed).

security.note: Unchanged: no credentials, no eval/exec of raw user strings, standard path-based file I/O only.

maintainability.note: Unchanged: clean modular separation; TF-IDF/SVD/clustering path re-confirmed bit-identical across unseeded reruns on this audit's own independent dataset.

agent_specific.note: Idempotency, previously flagged as 'chromVAR determinism not independently re-verified' (P2 in the prior audit), is now independently re-verified and FAILS: top-10 differential-motif overlap across 3 identical unseeded reruns was 3/10, 10/10, 10/10 (run1 vs run2/run3 diverges; run2 vs run3 agrees), and the count of p_adj<0.05 motifs swung 24 -> 4 -> 4. This directly costs points on the Idempotency sub-criterion; everything else in this category (trigger precision, line budget, composability) is unchanged.

inputs.label: Full workflow incl. the FIXED chromVAR block, TF ranking, and doublet detection
inputs.note: Central re-audit target. RunChromVAR() independently confirmed absent from the Signac 1.17.1 namespace (no exported symbol matches 'chromvar' at all). The fixed replacement block (addGCBias/matchMotifs/getBackgroundPeaks/computeDeviations) runs cleanly and produces a real 746-motif x 160-cell deviation matrix -- but re-running the IDENTICAL block 3 times on the IDENTICAL object, in the same session, with SKILL.md's documented code (no set.seed anywhere), gave 24, 4, and 4 significant (p_adj<0.05) motifs respectively, and only 3/10 overlap between run 1's and runs 2-3's top-10 differential-motif lists. Root cause isolated to chromVAR::getBackgroundPeaks(), which uses unseeded sampling (76.8% of its background-peak assignment matrix differs between two calls on the identical input); computeDeviations() itself is fully deterministic given identical background peaks. A set.seed() immediately before getBackgroundPeaks() makes the whole block perfectly reproducible (verified). This fires the T3 Skill Veto (Result Determinism: 'critical numerical results fluctuate randomly with each call').

key_strengths: Both P1s from the pre-fix audit are independently confirmed fixed: RunChromVAR() is genuinely absent from Signac 1.17.1's namespace (no exported symbol matches 'chromvar' at all) and the replacement chromVAR API sequence runs cleanly on an independent synthetic dataset the fixer never used; GetGRangesFromEnsDb() now succeeds using only the documented Prerequisites.

The fixer's decision NOT to add Rsamtools to Prerequisites is independently confirmed correct via the actual mechanism: Rsamtools is a Signac Imports dependency (auto-installed by install.packages('Signac')), while biovizBase is Signac Suggests-only (never auto-installed) -- exactly why one needed documenting and the other did not.

The core TF-IDF/LSI/depth-diagnosis/clustering pipeline remains empirically deterministic and correct on a fresh 3-cell-type dataset: ARI=1.0, and it correctly handles a genuinely harder edge case (two depth-correlated components, not one) that the pre-fix audit never exercised.

Differential accessibility (logistic regression with fragment depth as a latent variable) reproduced the same ~85% ground-truth overlap on an entirely independent synthetic dataset, indicating the DA method itself is robust rather than a lucky first run.
Motif!=TF and scope-boundary guardrails held under two new adversarial/scope probes this audit designed independently of the original audit's inputs.

recommendations.title: chromVAR's fixed replacement block is not reproducible across identical reruns -- fires the T3 Skill Veto
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's chromVAR Motif Deviations section (the section this fix pass just rewrote) has no set.seed() call anywhere. Running the documented addGCBias/matchMotifs/getBackgroundPeaks/computeDeviations sequence 3 times on the identical object gave 24, 4, and 4 significant motifs respectively, with only 3/10 overlap in the top-10 differential-motif list between run 1 and runs 2-3. This is 'critical numerical results fluctuate randomly with each call' (basic_veto.md T3.3), a hard Skill Veto gate.
recommendations.root_cause: chromVAR::getBackgroundPeaks() draws its GC-/accessibility-matched background peaks via unseeded R sampling; this predates the fix (the old RunChromVAR() wrapper called the same function internally) but was only flagged as an unverified P2 in the prior audit and is now independently confirmed to fail badly. computeDeviations() itself was confirmed fully deterministic given identical background peaks -- the randomness is isolated entirely to getBackgroundPeaks().
recommendations.fix: Add `set.seed(<fixed integer>)` immediately before the `getBackgroundPeaks()` call in SKILL.md's chromVAR block (verified in this audit: matching set.seed() calls before two invocations make the output byte-identical). Note in Version Compatibility or Common Errors that the seed is for reproducibility only, not a statistical assumption, and that a different seed will shift the exact ranking without changing top-hit stability meaningfully once N is large enough.
